# Appeal of Denial — Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination, dated 2026-08-11**
**Member: Sawyer Alvarez | Member ID: W635441117**
**Reference number: POC-A1F3D3C000-86797**
**Governing policy: Cigna Medical Coverage Policy 0285 Total Ankle Arthroplasty** ([link](https://static.cigna.com/assets/chcp/pdf/coveragePolicies/medical/mm_0285_coveragepositioncriteria_total_ankle_arthroplasty.pdf))

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), which Cigna denied on 2026-08-11 as not medically necessary. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this procedure is needed, and I am asking Cigna to reconsider this decision.

## Why I believe my records meet the plan's own criteria

Cigna's policy states that a total ankle arthroplasty using an FDA-approved/cleared device:

> "is considered medically necessary as an alternative to ankle arthrodesis when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

The specific criteria listed are that the condition:

> " is function-limiting at short distances (e.g., walking less than ¼ mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration  interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment • failure of at least six months of conservative therapy (i.e., anti-inflammatory medications, orthotic devices, activity modification, physical therapy) • individual has NONE of the following contraindications to total ankle arthroplasty:"

My records show each of these elements is met:

- **Function-limiting for at least three months:** My chart documents 12 months of progressive ankle pain, and I currently ambulate with an antalgic gait limited to two city blocks — the same distance the policy itself gives as an example of function-limiting impairment.
- **Failure of at least six months of conservative therapy:** I completed 18 visits of supervised physical therapy over 10 weeks (2026-04-18 to 2026-06-27), took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-29 that gave only two weeks of partial relief. This is documented conservative treatment exceeding six months, consistent with the policy's requirement.
- **No listed contraindications:** My records show no active infection and no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

Weight-bearing radiographs from 2026-06-02 show tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts, and exam findings include positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion — objective findings that support the level of impairment described above.

Cigna's policy also states:

> "Total Ankle Arthroplasty/Replacement/Revision Considered Medically Necessary when criteria in the applicable policy statements listed above are met:"

Because the record shows each of the criteria the policy sets out for using total ankle arthroplasty as an alternative to arthrodesis, I believe this procedure meets Cigna's own published standard for medical necessity.

## What I am asking

I ask that Cigna reverse this denial and approve coverage for the total ankle replacement (CPT 27702) recommended by my surgeon, Dr. Duval, based on the clinical documentation described above. If any additional records — such as the physical therapy discharge note, imaging report, or surgeon's operative plan — would help complete this review, please let me know what is needed and I will provide it or ask my surgeon's office to submit it.

## Deadline and how I am submitting this appeal

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-07. I am submitting it online through my.cigna.com and/or by calling 1-800-244-6224, and mailing a copy to the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

_______________________________
Sawyer Alvarez
Member ID: W635441117
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [date signed]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

0285 Revision total ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for moderate to severe ankle pain secondary to failure of an implanted device (e.g., implant loosening, malpositioning, periprosthetic infection, periprosthetic fracture).
Revision Surgery Revision surgery may be necessary in the presence of failed arthroplasty.
Failed arthroplasty is typically suspected when pain occurs progressively over time and is persistent, indicating implant loosening and collapse.
Surgical management of failed TAR may include ankle arthrodesi s, revision arthroplasty, or amputation.
Revision total ankle arthroplasty for any other indication is considered not medically necessary.

Where coverage for care or services does not depend on specific circumstances, reimbursement will only be provided if a requested service(s) is submitted in accordance with the relevant criteria outlined in the applicable Coverage Policy, including covered diagnosis and/or procedure code(s).
Total ankle arthroplasty/replacement for any other indication is considered not medically necessary.

Conservative management typically consists of medications for pain control, limiting activity, the use of ankle braces to stabilize the joint, shoe modifications, heat, and physical therapy to control the pain associated with ankle arthrosis.
When conservative management fails, ankle arthrodesis (AA) (fusion) has been the standard surgical treatment of choice to control the pain of severe ankle arthritis.
Treatment of early talar AVN may include conservative measures like non- or protective weightbearing, or joint-sparing procedures (e.g., core decompression, bone grafting).
